issues.situation:
The landing test assumes the unit moves further than the executor actually moves it. _ri_quarter_tier_move moves every model in a straight line by the full M (walk) or by M+3.5 (Advance), and it takes the walk whenever that lands wholly inside the quarter. The executor moves less:
- Every model is capped at 0.95 x the move (safe_move_px in _try_move_with_collision_check).
- The Normal-move path passes threat_data, so _find_safer_position keeps a 0.75x or 0.5x move whenever that saves more than 1.5 threat per inch lost. This is normal when stepping toward a contested flank objective.
- The Normal-move path also passes the weapon range, so _clamp_move_for_weapon_range (MOV-1) can shorten the walk further.
- An Advance is re-planned after the roll at 0.95 x (M+D6).
The finding itself shows this. Round 3's walk variant at s7437 (seeds 5001-5004: 0, -2, -11, -3) never scored the quarter. Yet an unshortened 8" walk puts every model centre about 0.7" past the halfway line, which the engine scores (model centres only). So the executed walk fell short. Units reinforcing a held centre stand near the halfway lines, so the walk branch will often be the one chosen, and any shortened walk repeats that -4 result: reinforcement given up, no quarter scored. The Advance branch is chosen exactly in the band where the walk fails and M+3.5 lands. There, roughly 1 fire in 5 misses on a roll of 1-3 (1 in 2 at the top of the band). The unit has then also lost its charge, and its shooting if its weapons are not [ASSAULT].
issues.proposed_change:
Make _ri_quarter_tier_move model the executor and the engine's scoring rule:
(a) Walk only if the unit lands wholly inside at 0.75 x 0.95 x M (the first _find_safer_position step).
(b) Otherwise Advance only if the unit lands at 0.95 x (M+2), so it lands on every roll of 2 or more. Or compute P(land) over the six rolls at 0.95 x (M+roll) and require at least 2/3.
(c) Test 'wholly within' the way the engine scores it (SecondaryMissionManager._is_unit_wholly_in_rect: model centres inside the quarter, base edge more than 6" from the centre), not with the stricter 'no base across a halfway line'.
The finding still fires: at s7437 the worst roll (9", executed 8.55") still puts every Beta base 19 px inside quarter 2, and the 0.75x walk does not land, so Beta still Advances.

issues.situation:
Quarter coverage ignores the plan's own moves. COORD-4 builds the movement plan once per phase from start-of-phase positions, and covered_others comes only from those snapshot positions. Three things are missed:
(a) Quarters that units assigned earlier in the same pass 2 will enter this turn. Under Recon Sweep the base already gives secondary_spread +4.2 to moves into an uncovered quarter, so a higher-scored unit is often assigned there first.
(b) Its own earlier redirects. After unit U is redirected, the held objective's need stays open. The next reinforcer V then passes the same test against the same still-uncovered quarter. Two or three reinforcers can be stripped off one held objective. The cascade only stops when the alternative objective's need is used up, and an enemy-held flank objective can need a lot (obj_nml_2 at s7437 needed about 11 OC).
(c) Quarters that assigned units leave this turn, which overstates the tier.
In (a) and (b) the extra redirect scores no tier and the held objective loses its reinforcement, which is strictly worse than base. Also, the moving unit's attached leader is a separate unit (for example Blade Champion C with Beta). It stays in 'others' and is counted as covering its current quarter, although it moves with the unit.
issues.proposed_change:
Keep a plan-level ri_quarters set for this pass:
- Seed it with _get_covered_quarters of units that do not move this phase, plus the pass-1 holders.
- Add the landing quarter of every move or advance assignment already made in pass 2 (same landing estimate as the fix).
- Add each redirect's quarter when it fires.
Compute the gain as tier(set + q) - tier(set) instead of using snapshot covered_others. Also erase the unit's attachment_data.attached_characters from 'others'. The finding still fires: at s7437 no other unit reaches quarter 2 this turn (Alpha's Advance ends near y 760).

issues.situation: The alternative loop scans the unit's candidates from the top of the score list and checks only 'still needs OC' and TOO-LATE. So it can pick the very candidate that LONE-TRIP (on in V9), RACE-SKIP or DIM-RETURNS skipped for this unit a moment earlier. It also never compares the alternative's score with the reinforcement's, and that score includes threat_delta, overwatch_risk and contest_race. Orks hold Recon Sweep in 4 of the 11 bench games where the fix can fire (98010, 97002, 97027, 97085). Their Gretchin (T2 W1) and Stormboyz (W1, M12) are LONE-TRIP-fragile. A redirect banks one +3 at end of turn and can then lose the unit in the enemy turn. Purge and Secure, the opponent's card in every Recon Sweep game, pays 3 VP for destroying a unit that started the turn on an objective. Round 1 measured not sending these lone fragile units as clear gains (+8.67, +4.78, +1.92).
issues.proposed_change: In the alternative filter add 'or lone_trip.call(alt)', and require alt.score > 0 (or alt.score >= cand.score - 25; the gap at s7437 is 17.5). Do not add race_hopeless: at s7437 the 3-turn race to obj_nml_2 counts as 'hopeless' (32 vs 14 OC), and that check would block the measured gain. Here the quarter matters, not the capture. Beta is T7 W5, so the LONE-TRIP filter does not affect the finding.

issues.situation: The redirect fires on any held objective, including our home. It also ignores the candidate's plan earmark. V9 added an earmark guard to the keeper release for authored plans, and LONE-TRIP and FAR-TRIP exempt home. In every bench Recon Sweep game the opponent plays Purge and Secure. It pays 4 VP per Command phase for each objective it controls outside its own home (our home counts), plus 3 VP for hold_new. So a home reinforcer redirected to score one quarter can give the opponent 4 VP every round. This is rare in the bench fixtures, because home is seldom threatened when the plan is built. It matters more against human players and with authored plans.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the REINFORCE-INSURANCE block when _get_obj_eval_by_id(obj_evaluations, oid).get('is_home', false) is true, or when str(cand.get('earmark', '')) != ''.

issues.situation: The alternative objective does not have to lie in the landing quarter. A unit that crosses an uncovered quarter on the way to an objective in another quarter (for example toward obj_home_2 through quarter 2) scores the tier once. It then walks out of that quarter next turn, yet it gave up the reinforcement for the whole enemy turn.
issues.proposed_change: Require _get_table_quarter(alt.objective_pos) == quarter. The finding still fires: at s7437 obj_nml_2 is in quarter 2, which is Beta's landing quarter.

issues.situation: The patch leaves in place an existing base bias toward the centre. The base secondary_spread term (+4.2 under a quarters card) takes the quarter from _get_table_quarter(estimated_dest). For a unit within M of the centre, estimated_dest lands on (880,1200), give or take float rounding. That function assigns this point to quarter 3 (strict '<' tests), or to another quarter by rounding. The centre can never count for a quarter, because it is within 6" of the centre. P1 rarely covers quarter 3, so under Recon Sweep every P1 unit that can reach the centre gets +4.2 for nothing. This pulls P1 reinforcers onto the centre, which is the behaviour this cluster is about.
issues.proposed_change: In the secondary_spread block, give no bonus when estimated_dest is within 6" plus the base radius of the board centre. This is a separate one-line fix; measure it on its own.

issues.situation: The standard bench cannot measure this fix (see fires_in_bench): at most 11 of 124 pairs per baseline can change, and about 3-6 will. The +19.0 full-game result is for a one-shot forced alternative, not for the fix firing again in rounds 3-5 of the same game, and the designer counted fires only to the end of the next round. Four of the six guardrails are not Recon Sweep games and the other two sit on the support or charge paths, so 'unchanged' there holds by construction and is not evidence that the fix is safe.
issues.proposed_change:
Measure it where it fires:
- Run paired side-swapped full games with --dispositions reconnaissance,take_and_hold and with take_and_hold,reconnaissance on all three fixtures. E then comes from the arm where the candidate holds Recon Sweep.
- Count [REINFORCE_INSURANCE] log lines per game.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Rarely, and too seldom for the bench to measure. Only Reconnaissance Sweep has end-of-turn 'quarters' rules. With --rules11e the bench deals dispositions from the seed (P1 = DISPOSITIONS[s%5], P2 = DISPOSITIONS[(s/5)%5]). So P1 gets Recon Sweep when s is 2 mod 25, P2 gets it when s is 10 mod 25, and the opponent always plays Purge and Secure.

With the round-3 seed sets (cus 96001-14/21-34/41-54, asy 98001-14/21-34/41-54, ork 97001-08/21-28/41-48/61-68/81-88; +500 for the V0 runs), 11 of 124 pairs per baseline are eligible:
- cus: 96002, 96010, 96027, 96052
- asy: 98002, 98010, 98027, 98052
- ork: 97002, 97027, 97085

In each of these, only the arm where the candidate holds the Recon Sweep seat can change: 11 of 248 games, about 4.4%.

Within those games, the trigger is checked when the plan is built (once per phase, from start-of-phase positions). It needs a held_threatened objective with positive need, a unit reinforcing it, and that unit able to land wholly in an uncovered quarter that raises the tier. I expect almost no fires in round 1: when P1 plans, only its home is held (need 0), and P2's home is rarely threatened. Fires are plausible in rounds 2-4. In the Ork mirror each side starts with 2 quarters, so the third quarter is easier to reach there.

Base rate: held-objective reinforcements are about 2% of critic-flagged movement decisions (7 of 317; 1 of the 39 under Recon Sweep, which is s7437).

My estimate is about 0.3-0.6 fires per eligible game, so about 3-6 changed pairs per baseline and at least 95% identical pairs. Even at the s7437 full-game size (+19 per changed game, about +9.5 E per pair), pooled E moves by only about +0.2 to +0.5 VP, which is below the bench's resolution. It cannot fire at s7451 (Search and Scour card, pass-3 support path, and a same-objective Advance question).
reviews.strengths:
- It targets the mechanism the evidence supports. Round 3's A/B records traced the gain to Recon Sweep 'quarters +3' at end of rounds 2 and 3.
- At s7437 it makes exactly the measured alternative (Beta Advances to obj_nml_2), which is the cluster's best-evidenced change: +4.36 [0.61, 8.12] over 36 seeds and +19.0 [3.3, 34.7] over 12 full games. The finding is robust under the executor: any Advance roll clears the line by at least 0.9", while the walk misses by 0.07".
- It fires only under Recon Sweep, and FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE=0 restores base exactly. The patch applies cleanly to 5e70bc2.
- It does not use round 3's dropped COORD-5 threat model, and it never touches charges, so it respects the s7418 r3 -8.33 guardrail.
- The tier gain subtracts the unit's own current quarter: a unit that alone covers its quarter gains 0.
- It prefers a Normal move when that is enough.
- It writes a [REINFORCE_INSURANCE] log line, a coordination note on the unit's card, and an assign_pass that OBJ-BACKFILL-1 respects.
reviews.summary:
The narrow design is sound in direction and tightly scoped. Under Reconnaissance Sweep, a reinforcement of a held objective gives way to a move that completes a quarter tier, and at the finding it reproduces the best-measured alternative in this cluster.

Through the game-impact lens, the risk sits in the few games where it fires:
1. Its landing test assumes the unit moves further than the executor really moves it (full M or M+3.5 in a straight line, versus the 0.95 cap, threat-aware 0.75/0.5 shortening and the MOV-1 clamp on walks, and the D6 on Advances). Some fires therefore give up the reinforcement without scoring the quarter. That is the -4 'walk' outcome measured at s7437 itself.
2. Its quarter coverage ignores the plan's own moves, because the plan is built once per phase from start-of-phase positions. It can send a reinforcer into a quarter another assigned unit already takes, or strip several reinforcers off one held objective. Both are strictly worse than base.

Both fixes are cheap and keep s7437 firing. I also recommend the LONE-TRIP filter, the home and earmark exemptions, and the same-quarter objective check. It does not help s7451. The standard bench can change at most 11 of 124 pairs per baseline (about 3-6 expected), so it will mostly show identical pairs; measure it with forced Recon Sweep dispositions.

Verdict: revise. I did not run Godot. The findings come from reading the 5e70bc2 code (AIDecisionMaker, AIPlayer, MissionManager, SecondaryMissionManager) and from geometry on the saved positions. The scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/ri_narrow_gamerev/ (quarters.py, beta_margin.py, scan_cases.py). That scratchpad is shared with sibling agents. I also wrote base_AIDM.gd there, possibly over an existing copy, but every base_*.gd copy there is byte-identical to 5e70bc2, so nothing was lost.

issues.situation: _ri_quarter_tier_move builds `others` by erasing only unit_id, so the mover's attached CHARACTER units are counted as if they stay in their current quarter. Examples: a Blade Champion attached to Custodian Guard, a Warboss or Nob leading Boyz; both bench armies have many. The engine moves them with the bodyguard: MovementPhase.get_available_actions skips units with attached_to, and _move_attached_characters translates them. When the bodyguard and its leader are the only presence in their quarter, the helper credits a tier that will not happen. I re-implemented the helper in Python and ran it on a synthetic board: q0 holds one squad; q1 holds only bodyguard D plus attached leader L; D's alt move toward obj_home_2 lands wholly in q3. The helper returns now 2, new 3, gain +3 (both move and advance). The true result is still 2 quarters, gain 0. The gate then drops the reinforcement of a threatened held objective (and, in Advance mode, the unit's shooting and charge) for nothing. The finding is not affected: at s7437 Blade Champion C is attached to Beta, and excluding it still gives covered_others [T,T,F,F] and +3.
issues.proposed_change: In _ri_quarter_tier_move, after others.erase(unit_id), also erase every id in unit.get("attachment_data", {}).get("attached_characters", []). Those units move with the bodyguard and end in its quarter. Add a test: the redirect candidate plus an attached leader are the only cover of a quarter, so there is no redirect. Keep the s7437-shape case, which is unchanged by this fix.

issues.situation: The movement plan is built once per Movement phase (COORD-4 _turn_movement_plan) and then consumed unit by unit. The helper, however, reads quarter coverage from the start-of-plan snapshot. So it cannot see (a) its own earlier redirect in the same pass 2, or (b) an earlier pass-1/pass-2 move/advance assignment whose move this turn already lands a unit wholly in that quarter. A later unit's reinforcement candidate then sees the quarter as still uncovered and is credited the same +3 tier, and is redirected again whenever the alt objective still needs OC. The need check does not prevent this. At s7437, obj_nml_2's need is about 11 (Lootas project 10 OC, PROJECTED_NEED_CAP 4 x scale 2.55 = 10), above Custodian Guard Beta's 9 OC, so a second redirect toward it would pass. Result: two reinforcements (or one plus a redundant capture) are given up for one tier. This is rarer than the attached-leader case. Under Reconnaissance Sweep, the base's flat +4.2 secondary_spread bonus already sends units into uncovered quarters, which makes variant (b) plausible. No independent second unit qualifies at s7437, so the finding is unaffected.
issues.proposed_change: In pass 2, keep planned_q = [false, false, false, false]. Set planned_q[ri_move.quarter] = true after each redirect. Preferably also set it for each hold/move/advance assignment made earlier in this plan whose straight-line landing (the helper's own landing loop, in the assignment's mode) is wholly inside a quarter. Pass planned_q into _ri_quarter_tier_move. Inside, count now_count over (covered by all units) OR planned_q, set covered_others = (covered by others) OR planned_q, and set new_count = 1 + count(covered_others). Add a test with two independent units that can each complete the third quarter while the alt objective's need exceeds the first unit's OC: only the first is redirected and the second reinforces.

issues.situation: Advance landing assumes M + 3.5" (ADVANCE_EXPECTED_EXTRA_INCHES). The executor plans BEGIN_ADVANCE destinations at M + 2". The real roll is used only when the advance pauses for a Command Re-roll decision (_execute_pending_advance_move). Without that pause (0 CP, or re-roll unavailable), the M+2 destinations are staged as they are. On a roll of 1 that staging fails, and AIPlayer falls back to 0.75 x M, which is shorter than a Normal move. Where the needed extra is 2-3.5", the gate can trade the reinforcement for a quarter that is reached about half the time.
issues.proposed_change: Test the Advance landing at move_in + 2.0, the executor's own planning distance, or require that the minimum roll needed is 2 or less. At s7437 the Advance still lands with a 1.9" margin at +2 (and 0.4" at +0.5), so the finding is kept.

issues.situation: The gate fires on any held_threatened reinforcement. That includes objectives where enemy OC is already in control range (the reinforcement keeps control now; it is not insurance). It also includes an objective that is our only non-home hold for Reconnaissance Sweep's hold_min rule (3 VP each command phase, rounds 2-5): there, losing the objective costs as much as the quarter gains, before secondaries.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the redirect when eval.enemy_oc > 0, or when this objective is the only non-home objective we hold that the card's hold_min rule counts. Optionally also skip our home objective when a secondary values it (defend_home). Both guards keep the s7437 fire: centre enemy OC in range was 0, and obj_nml_1 was held with OC 11.

issues.situation: Executor fidelity and cost of the chosen mode: (1) Advance mode ignores lost shooting for non-[ASSAULT] ranged weapons and the lost charge. That is free for Beta's Guardian Spear, but not for Lootas, Devastators and similar units. (2) Move mode predicts a straight walk that stops at control range. The Normal-move executor instead blends the target toward a charge-intent target (70/30), a half-range point, or a point that keeps shooting targets. It can also REMAIN_STATIONARY to shoot or for the Heavy bonus, so a 'move' hit can miss the quarter entirely.
issues.proposed_change: Accept 'advance' only when the unit has no non-ASSAULT ranged weapon with a target in range now (reuse the _should_unit_advance shooting test). Accept 'move' only when the unit has no charge intent and no ranged targets in range. Otherwise require the Advance landing, whose executor path heads straight to the objective.

issues.situation: The redirect target bypasses the pass-2 vetoes that the alt would face on its own (DIM-RETURNS reprice skip, RACE-SKIP, LONE-TRIP). It is applied through apply_capture_assignment, which consumes that objective's OC need and adds it to planned_new_objs, so the redirect also changes other units' DIM-RETURNS pricing. The assignment also keeps walk-pace race data: turns_to_reach 3 and 'racing for it ... before we arrive in 3 turns' after the action becomes an Advance that arrives in 2.
issues.proposed_change: Run lone_trip and race_hopeless on the alt, as overcommit_redirect does. If the quarter alone should justify the redirect even onto a hopeless objective, say so in the reason. When switching to 'advance', recompute turns_to_reach and drop the walk-pace race narration.

issues.situation: Report accuracy. (1) Finding 2 (s7418 r1 p2) is described as 'P2 Orks, Take and Hold card, no quarter rule'. P2's card is Reconnaissance Sweep (dispositions P1 take_and_hold, P2 reconnaissance). The gate leaves it unchanged only because that decision ('reinforcing obj_nml_2 (1 unit already committed)') comes from the pass-3 support fallback (_find_best_remaining_objective), which the gate does not touch. (2) Four of the six guardrails (s7417, s7431, s7438, s7424) can never fire, because neither player has a quarters card. Only s7418 r2/r3 (P2 on Reconnaissance Sweep) actually test the gate. (3) The new s7451 evidence is out of scope: P2's card there is Search and Scour, the decision comes from the support pass, and the measured alternative is an Advance to the same objective.
issues.proposed_change: Correct the finding-2 reasoning. State that only s7418 r2/r3 exercise the gate among the guardrails. Say plainly that the design does not address s7451 or the [ASSAULT]-aware Advance direction.

issues.situation: Test fidelity. _plan() sets _primary_awareness_p1 with "quarters": false and objective_pressure 0 while passing quarter rules. The real Reconnaissance Sweep awareness sets quarters true, which adds the flat 4.2 secondary_spread bonus: exactly the base term this fix competes with. The house test (keeper_release) uses the same pattern. In the walk test, the first branch passes on any obj_nml_2 assignment even if the gate never fired. There are no cases for the two counting bugs above.
issues.proposed_change: Set quarters: true (and objective_pressure / kill_pressure as _build_primary_awareness would for these rules), and re-check that the base still reinforces. Make the walk test assert assign_pass == 'reinforce_insurance' and action 'move' unconditionally. Add the attached-leader case and the two-redirect case.

issues.situation: Nits. The player-facing reason says 'into table quarter %d', exposing the internal 0-3 index. 'held_safe' in the gate's state list is unreachable, because _initial_objective_oc_needs gives held_safe a pass-2 need of 0. now_count and covered_others do not depend on the alt but are recomputed for every alt.
issues.proposed_change: Print a quarter name (top-left / top-right / bottom-left / bottom-right). Drop held_safe, or comment that it is unreachable. Compute the two coverage arrays once per gate call and pass them in.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Rarely. The gate fires only for a seat whose primary has eot 'quarters' rules, which in practice means Reconnaissance Sweep (reconnaissance played vs take_and_hold). The bench picks dispositions by seed: P1 = DISPOSITIONS[s%5], P2 = DISPOSITIONS[(s/5)%5]. So a seat has that card only for seeds ≡ 2 (P1) or ≡ 10 (P2) mod 25, about 2 of every 25 seed pairs. In each such pair only one game has the candidate in that seat (arm M2 for ≡2, M1 for ≡10). Inside such a game it also needs a pass-2 reinforcement of a held_threatened objective (held_safe never has pass-2 need) that a unit could swap for a move completing the 3rd or 4th quarter. In the Crucible fixtures the Custodes start covering 1 quarter and the Orks 2, so this is mostly R2-R3. Of the 301 measured positions, 40 have the decider on Reconnaissance Sweep, and only one of those, s7437 r2 p1, is a pass-2 held reinforcement. My estimate is about 0-1 fires per eligible game. That gives roughly 1-4 differing pairs in a 64-72 pair bench (3 fixtures x ~21-24 seeds), with at least ~94% of pairs identical. Even a +10 VP effect in the affected games would average under +0.5 VP per pair, so the bench cannot resolve it. To measure it, run fixed-disposition arms (--dispositions reconnaissance,take_and_hold and take_and_hold,reconnaissance) on the asym and mirror fixtures, so every game is eligible.
reviews.strengths: This is the smallest rule change in the cluster, and it is aimed at the mechanism the evidence supports: the Reconnaissance Sweep quarter tier, not a threat model. It does not repeat the dropped REINFORCE-CAP premise and does not veto holders' charges. FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE=0 restores base decisions exactly: ri_on short-circuits the only call site, the helper is unreachable otherwise, the patch removes no lines, and get_param only records the read. At the finding it reproduces exactly the alternative that was measured: same unit, obj_nml_2, Advance; +4.36 [0.61, 8.12] over 36 seeds and +19.0 over 12 full games. My Python re-implementation of the helper on the decoded s7437 save confirms the report. P1 covers quarters 0 and 1. Beta's 8\" walk ends with bases 0.07\" across the halfway line. Any Advance roll of 1 or more lands it wholly in quarter 2 (margin 0.4-4.6\"), taking the count from 2 to 3 quarters (+3). The halfway-line base check is stricter than the engine scorer (model centres only) but faithful to 'wholly within', and it is what makes the design choose Advance there. The redirect is tagged assign_pass 'reinforce_insurance', so OBJ-BACKFILL-1 does not switch it back, and it adds a [REINFORCE_INSURANCE] log line plus a coordination note. Cost is negligible: the helper returns at once without a quarters rule, and otherwise does two coverage scans per alt. The test pins and erases the override and drives the real planner (_evaluate_all_objectives + _assign_units_to_objectives). It fails on base for the right reason (Beta reinforces the centre), and has negative cases for no quarter card, no tier gain, and a covered quarter.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: revise. The idea is sound for its narrow scope, and it reproduces the measured s7437 alternative exactly. But the quarter count it relies on has two real counting bugs. Both have small fixes, and both fixes keep the s7437 fire.

1. Attached leaders (major). _ri_quarter_tier_move counts the mover's attached leader as staying in its current quarter. The engine actually moves attached characters with their bodyguard, and such leaders are common in both bench armies. On a synthetic board where a bodyguard and its leader are the only cover of a quarter, the helper reports +3 for a move that leaves the count at 2. The gate would then drop a threatened reinforcement for nothing. Fix: also erase attachment_data.attached_characters from `others`.

2. Plan-blind coverage (major). The movement plan is built once per phase, but the helper reads coverage from the snapshot. A later redirect, or an earlier capture into the same quarter, is credited the same tier again. At s7437 obj_nml_2's need (~11) exceeds Beta's OC (9), so the need check does not stop a second redirect toward it. Fix: track the quarters this plan already fills and treat them as covered.

Minor issues:
- The Advance landing uses M+3.5, but the executor stages M+2 when no re-roll pause happens. Use M+2.
- It also fires when enemy OC is already in range, or when the objective is the card's only hold_min objective. Add guards.
- Advance and move ignore shooting and charge costs and the normal-move executor's blends.
- The redirect target skips LONE-TRIP and RACE-SKIP, and keeps walk-pace race narration after switching to Advance.
- Test fidelity: quarters:false in the awareness, a lenient walk test, and no tests for either bug.
- Nits: a 0-3 quarter index in player text, and an unreachable held_safe check.

Report check:
- The finding-1 decision check matches the code and my re-implementation.
- The finding-2 reasoning is wrong: P2's card at s7418 is Reconnaissance Sweep, not Take and Hold. It is unchanged only because that decision comes from the pass-3 support fallback.
- Four of the six guardrails cannot fire at all (no quarters card for either player). Only s7418 r2/r3 test the gate.
- The design cannot help s7451 (Search and Scour; support-pass decision; the alternative is an Advance to the same objective).
- It fires in only about 1-4 of 64-72 bench pairs, so the bench cannot measure it. Use fixed Reconnaissance Sweep disposition arms instead.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Often: not narrow, unlike the report's '1 of 25 pairings'. Estimated from data and code; I did not run any games. It triggers when the decider holds Recon Sweep or Engage on All Fronts. Recon Sweep: dispositions follow the seed (P1=D[s%5], P2=D[(s//5)%5]). In the round-3 bench seed layout that is 11 of 124 pairs: cus 96002/96027/96052 (P1) and 96010 (P2); asy 98002/98027/98052 (P1) and 98010 (P2); ork 97002/97027 (P1) and 97085 (P2). The candidate holds Recon Sweep in one game of each of these pairs. EoAF is far more common. It is an 18-card 11e tactical deck with 2 draws per turn, and EoAF stays in hand until achieved, so a player has drawn it by round r with probability about 2r/18 (~56% by R5). In the round-3 bench EoAF was scored about 0.5-0.8 times per game (2.6/2.7/1.8 VP per game in asy/cus/ork). In the older 11e Custodes-mirror season a quarter-card term was active in 57% of player-games and in 23% (R1) to 45% (R5) of movement phases. Whenever the trigger holds, the patch removes the flat 4.2/6.0 bonus from every candidate, which can change close calls. The quarter_vp term itself needs other units to cover 2+ quarters: Orks from deployment, Custodes usually from R2. It appears on at least one candidate in 32 of 275 saved sweep movement positions (R1 2%, R2 16%, R3 28%), 21 of them through EoAF alone. My estimate: roughly half of the bench pairs or more will stop being identical, and about two-thirds of the changed decisions will come from EoAF rather than from the Recon Sweep case the evidence supports. If restricted to the primary as proposed, it would fire in about 11 of 124 pairs.
reviews.strengths: It finds the real causes at s7437: the only quarter term was a flat 4.2 bonus, presence was never checked (a walk stops on the quarter line), RACE-1 ignored [ASSAULT], and RACE-SKIP vetoed the candidate. It reproduces the measured alternative exactly (Beta Advances to obj_nml_2), and that alternative has the cluster's only full-game confirmation (+19.0 over 12 games). The presence test matches the scorer: every model wholly in one quarter, more than 6" from the centre, with the unit's footprint. Pricing is marginal on the tier, so a quarter another unit already covers and points near the centre get nothing; this removes real errors in the old flat bonus. Advance conversion happens only when it is free (no enemy within M+12", only [ASSAULT] guns or nothing in range), so it never gives up a charge. It never vetoes charges: _melee_chase_gate does not read plan scores, so the s7418 r3 guardrail (-8.33) is safe, and all 5 checked guardrails are unchanged. LONE-TRIP and DIM-RETURNS still apply, and FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE=0 restores the base exactly. Unlike V9's keeper fix, it fires in the bench, so the bench can measure it.
reviews.summary: For Reconnaissance Sweep, a primary that pays every turn, the idea is right and backed by evidence: s7437 +4.36 over 36 seeds and +19.0 over 12 full games. But the design also gives Engage on All Fronts the same every-turn persistence. In the bench EoAF is a tactical card that pays 3/5 VP once and is discarded, so a one-time 3 VP is priced at 21-31.5 points in R1-R3. EoAF is held in roughly half of all games, so it drives most of the design's effect in the bench. The only measured EoAF position where the term changes which option scores higher goes the wrong way: at s7454 r3 P2 (Custodes mirror, V9), keeping Gamma in its quarter instead of Advancing to the centre measured 21.5 VP worse, and the design adds +21 to that worse move. The RACE-SKIP/TOO-LATE exemption also lets EoAF-only value send units into hopeless races. The design does not touch s7451: no quarter card is held there, and the walk comes from the support pass. Revise: limit QUARTER-VP and the veto exemption to the primary's quarters rule, keeping EoAF on the base path (or price EoAF as a one-shot with no exemption), and add s7454 as a guardrail. The narrowed design fires in about 11 of 124 bench pairs.

issues.situation: Engage on All Fronts (EoAF) is priced as if it paid every turn. The code computes qv_score = gain x qv_persist x QUARTER_VP_WEIGHT (patched AIDecisionMaker.gd ~9951), so every group is multiplied by 1 + 0.5 x (5 - round). The bench plays the 11e TACTICAL deck. There EoAF scores once and is then discarded: SecondaryMissionManager._award_mission_vp marks it achieved and _discard_achieved_missions removes it in tactical mode. Result: at R1/R2/R3/R4 the 3rd quarter is worth 31.5/26.25/21/15.75 points. On the design's own 3.5 points/VP scale, 3 VP paid once is worth ~10.5. Every unit that is the only one in its quarter gets the same inflated 'stay' value. The tiers are hard-coded to the tactical values (3/5); fixed mode pays 2/4. This path fires in the bench at least as often as the Recon Sweep path the evidence supports. In the stored 224-game 11e season (bench_data/ai_versions_11e_2026-10-29) the candidate seat drew EoAF in 18 of 112 pairs (16%). Draws by round: R1 6, R2 7, R3 17, R4 7, R5 16. It was also active at guardrail s7438 r3 P2 (Punishment + engage_on_all_fronts), which the report does not mention. No measured finding supports the EoAF valuation.
issues.proposed_change: Give each group its own persistence. The primary eot 'quarters' group (Recon Sweep) keeps qv_persist. For EoAF, use persistence 1.0 with tiers 3/5 when SecondaryMissionManager.get_mode(player) == 'tactical', and qv_persist with tiers 2/4 in fixed mode. Simplest alternative: build qv_groups from the primary only, and gate the old EoAF flat bonus on 'EoAF not in qv_groups' instead of 'not qv_on'. That keeps the change inside the evidenced Recon Sweep case. Add a test: with EoAF tactical at R2, the 3rd-quarter candidate gets 3 x 1 x 3.5 = 10.5.

issues.situation: A unit's own attached leader is counted as another unit covering its quarter. Per unit, qv_units = snapshot.units minus unit_id only (~9471). An attached CHARACTER is a separate unit entry with its own model position. In the s7437 save, U_BLADE_CHAMPION_C has attached_to = U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B (Beta) and stands at (539,1000). The leader moves with its bodyguard (MovementPhase: 'Attached character moves with its bodyguard unit'). 3 of the 4 Custodian Guard squads are led, Beta included, and so are the Ork Beast Snagga Boyz and Kommandos. Effect (a): a led squad that is the only presence in quarter q sees q as covered by its own leader. Staying gets 0 quarter_vp and leaving costs nothing, so the report's 'durable' stay value never applies to led units, including Beta from R3 on. Effect (b): when the squad moves into another uncovered quarter, base_n still counts the quarter it leaves. A move that does not change the tier is priced as a full tier: 26.25 at R2, plus the RACE-SKIP/TOO-LATE exemption. Together, a led squad alone in a quarter prefers to leave it for another uncovered quarter by about 26 points. In Recon Sweep Custodes games the AI will move squads between quarters for no VP, possibly onto lost races.
issues.proposed_change: In the per-unit QUARTER-VP block, also remove the unit's attached characters (for att in unit.get('attachment_data', {}).get('attached_characters', []): qv_units.erase(att)) and any unit embarked in it. Add a test: a led squad alone in quarter 2 keeps quarter_vp on its candidates that stay in quarter 2, and gets none for moving to uncovered quarter 3.

issues.situation: The Advance end point uses the mean roll (M + 3.5", ADVANCE_EXPECTED_EXTRA_INCHES) and gives the quarter its full value. The executor plans Advance destinations at M + 2" (_select_movement_action ~7073). It re-plans to M + the real roll only when the Command Re-roll pause happens (AIPlayer._execute_pending_advance_move). With no CP, or the re-roll already used, the unit moves at most M + 2". So a quarter that needs a 4+ is worth about half its value, and without the pause it is not reached at all. At s7437 the need is ~1.9" (83%), so the finding is not affected.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
The fix is active for the candidate seat in about a quarter of the pairs.

Recon Sweep comes from 2 of the 25 disposition pairings: seed % 25 == 2 (P1) or == 10 (P2), i.e. seeds 9102, 9110, 9127, 9135, 9152, 9160. That is 2 of 21 or 4 of 42 pairs per fixture, in one game of each pair, every round.

Engage on All Fronts is active for the candidate seat in about 16% of pairs (18 of 112 in the stored 224-game 11e season), mostly drawn in R3-R5 and held for 1-2 turns.

In those turns, every candidate whose end point changes quarter status gets a new score. The flat 4.2/6.0 bonus is removed and 15.75-31.5 points for a tier are added. So I expect roughly 15-25% of pairs to be non-identical: about 3-5 of 21 or 6-10 of 42 pairs per fixture. The Engage on All Fronts path, which no finding supports and which is over-valued, probably produces as many of those as the Recon Sweep path.

Logged fires (Advance conversion, RACE-SKIP/TOO-LATE exemption, quarter take) should cluster in Recon Sweep games with Custodes seats. Every Custodes ranged weapon is [ASSAULT], so the free-Advance conversion is open to any Custodes unit with no enemy within M+12". Among the Orks only the Warbikers and the Wartrike qualify.

reviews.strengths:
- It goes after the mechanism actually measured at s7437: the 3-quarter Recon Sweep tier, a walk that stops on the quarter line, RACE-1 ignoring [ASSAULT], and the RACE-SKIP veto. The decision check matches the alternative exactly (same unit, obj_nml_2, Advance), and the score arithmetic checks out.
- It does not repeat the dropped REINFORCE-CAP: there is no threat model on the held objective and no charge veto, so the s7418 r3 guardrail is respected.
- The presence test mirrors the scorer conservatively: the footprint must be wholly inside one quarter and more than 6" from the centre. The objective VP estimator does not price "quarters", so nothing is counted twice.
- Param 0 restores base behaviour exactly; every changed path is gated. The code is null-safe and the format strings are correct.
- It is cheap: the per-unit work runs once per movement-phase plan, and it is cheaper than base whenever a quarter card is active.
- Log lines carry the [REINFORCE_INSURANCE] tag and no log line is removed.
- The test drives the real planner, pins and erases the override, and fails on base because beta does not Advance into the quarter.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: revise. The idea is sound and well matched to the s7437 evidence: price table-quarter presence at the card's VP, and let a unit Advance for free into the quarter when its guns are [ASSAULT] and nothing is in charge reach. But two real bugs need fixing before a bench run.

1. **Engage on All Fronts is valued as durable.** The persistence multiplier (up to 3.0 at R1) applies to all quarter cards. In the bench's tactical deck this card is scored once and discarded, so the term is 1.5-3x too large from R1 to R4. This path is active for the candidate seat in about 16% of pairs, at least as often as the evidenced Recon Sweep path (8% of pairs). It was also active at guardrail s7438 r3 without the report saying so.
2. **A unit's own attached leader counts as another unit in its quarter.** This affects Beta and 2 other Custodian Guard squads, and the Ork Boyz and Kommandos. A led squad that is the only unit in a quarter gets no value for staying, and gets a full tier (about 26 points plus the race-veto exemption) for moving to another quarter that adds nothing. In Recon Sweep games the Custodes would move squads between quarters for no VP.

Smaller issues:
- The second-unit claim check compares against options the unit cannot take.
- The race exemption ignores the claim.
- The Advance is valued at the mean roll, while the executor plans M+2".
- The test does not cover the exemption that the s7437 flip depends on.
- The LONE-TRIP doc comment is detached and the decision card shows the wrong reason.

Not affected by these issues: param-0 exactness, null safety, cost, logging, the s7437 decision arithmetic (52.8 = 30.7 − 4.2 + 26.25) and the geometry (an Advance roll of 2+ reaches quarter 2). The design does not fire at s7451, the new evidence.

All of this comes from reading the code and the saves. I did not run Godot, so the 9/0 test result and the replay numbers are the designer's claims.

issues.situation: One switch (FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE) turns on three unrelated changes, and in the bench they fire at very different rates. RI-ASSAULT changes Custodian Guard movement when a long trip starts with the nearest enemy centroid 18-24" away. In the bench data that is CG M6 with a 24" [ASSAULT] Guardian spear. I scanned 421 saved movement positions: unmoved CG were in that band in 7% of R1 decisions, 29% of R2 and 17% of R3. RI-RACE is the reinforcement logic this cluster is about, and it met its gate in only 4 of the 421 positions: 2 of 47 Custodes-vs-Orks (s7437 r2 p1, s7415 r3 p2), 0 of 120 Custodes mirror, 0 of 50 Orks mirror, 0 of 70 Orks-vs-Custodes. RI-QUARTER runs only when the decider's primary is Reconnaissance Sweep, which is 2 of the 25 bench pairings. So the bench result will be almost entirely a verdict on the [ASSAULT] Advance rule. A loss there throws away the s7437 fix with it. A gain ships RI-RACE and RI-QUARTER without a measurement. The round-3 review asked for each fix to be measured on its own, and the designer's own risk 1 says RI-ASSAULT needs a full-game arm. Also, the RI-ASSAULT line prints on every call, including calls where base would Advance anyway, so a log count does not count changed decisions.
issues.proposed_change: Give each part its own parameter: FIX_RI_RACE, FIX_RI_ASSAULT and FIX_RI_QUARTER, each defaulting to 1. FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE=0 should still turn all three off. In the Custodes mirror and the asymmetric fixture, run switch-off arms: all on vs RI-ASSAULT off, and all on vs RI-RACE off. In _should_unit_advance_long_trip, return early and print the RI-ASSAULT line only when an enemy centroid is within max_weapon_range, which is the only case where base would refuse, so the line counts real changes.

issues.situation: RI-RACE on 11e terrain-hosted objectives. All five bench objectives are hosted by terrain areas. The area-large pieces reach 6.7" from the marker and the centre trapezoids reach 7.6". eval.enemy_oc already counts enemy models standing on the hosting area (FIX_HELD_DUP). _ri_enemy_next_move_oc decides 'already in range' and reach by marker distance minus 3.79". So an enemy unit on the far part of the area is counted twice: once in enemy_oc and again as a next-move threat. COORD-5 avoids this with _unit_in_objective_range. Reach along the long side of the area is also underestimated. Enemy reach is measured from the nearest model, but our 1-move arrivals come from centroids, which tilts the 1.5 ratio toward 'lost'.
issues.proposed_change: Pass the objective's board entry to _ri_enemy_next_move_oc. Skip any unit for which _unit_in_objective_range(e_unit, hd_obj, hd_mm) is true, as COORD-5 does. Measure each model's gap with MissionManager.model_gap_to_objective_range_px instead of marker distance minus CR. Measure our 1-move arrivals the same nearest-model way.

issues.situation: RI-RACE's premise and timing. At s7437 itself, the round-3 replays found that base's Beta reinforcement kept the centre in the seeds where the Allarus charged off it. So 'the reinforcement cannot keep it' was false there, and the measured gain came from the Recon Sweep quarter. The 0.5 factor also applies to the whole candidate score, including value that is paid at the end of OUR turn, before the enemy moves. Examples are the Centre Ground secondary (3/5 VP at end of turn, which P1 had and lost in a round-3 replay) and hold_central end-of-turn primaries (Immovable Object, Search and Scour). When the holders charge off, the reinforcement is the unit that scores these.
issues.proposed_change: Apply MOVE_RACE_LOSS_FACTOR only to the command-phase hold value. Or skip RI-RACE on the central objective while an end-of-your-turn central rule is active for the decider (a hold_central eot primary rule, or Centre Ground).

issues.situation: RI-RACE is inconsistent with nearby logic. A 1-move capture or contest of an uncontrolled, contested or enemy_weak objective gets no race test at all. A reinforcement of 2 or more turns uses RACE-1's centroid reach. So RI-RACE can send the close unit away while a farther unit, arriving after the enemy's move, takes the same need, or while a capture under the same or a larger threat goes ahead. It is rare (4 of 421 positions), so the cost is bounded.
issues.proposed_change: When RI-RACE fires on an objective, price the 2+-turn reinforcements of that objective with the same nearest-model threat. Or apply the next-move test to every 1-move candidate, not only to held_threatened ones.

issues.situation: RI-QUARTER values the quarter step per unit, against a static coverage. The plan is built once per Movement phase. _ri_quarter_vp credits only the quarter that completes a tier, so going from 1 quarter to 2 is worth 0. In the bench Custodes fixtures every Custodes unit starts wholly in one quarter (P1 in Q0, P2 in Q3). So under Reconnaissance Sweep every round-1 candidate gets 0, where base gave +4.2 toward any uncovered quarter, and the 3-quarter R1 end-of-turn score (3 VP) is left to chance. reviews.summary: Verdict: revise. The direction is sound, and the design fixes its own finding: s7437 Beta Advances to obj_nml_2, which matches the measured alternative (+4.36 n36; +19.0 n12 full games). RI-RACE, the reinforcement logic this cluster is about, met its gate in only 4 of 421 saved movement positions, and RI-QUARTER runs only under Reconnaissance Sweep (about 8% of seeds). (b) RI-RACE's 'cannot keep it' premise was false at s7437 itself (base kept the centre there), and it halves value that is paid at the end of our own turn. (d) RI-ASSAULT prices threat at the walking spot. The design does not fire at s7451, where the walk comes from the pass-3 support move. Its replay evidence used the 11e Custodes data and Orks_2000, not the bench fixtures' data. Read-only review: I did not run Godot. My frequency numbers come from a Python re-implementation over the saved positions (statline OC, marker-distance range); it reproduces the designer's s7437 numbers exactly. issues.situation: RI-RACE's threat count (_ri_enemy_next_move_oc) ignores 11e hosting areas. Every objective in the 3 bench fixtures and at s7437 has source_pieces hosting areas: 7x11.5" rectangles, and two 8x11.5" trapezoids for the centre, reaching 6.7-7.6" from the marker. FIX_HELD_DUP is on, so eval.enemy_oc counts any model whose base overlaps the area. The helper uses the marker point instead, which causes three errors. (a) It treats a unit as already counted only when a model is within 3.79" of the marker. An enemy unit standing on the area but more than 3.79" from the marker is therefore counted twice: once in enemy_oc and again in full as a next-move arrival. COORD-5 in _evaluate_all_objectives excludes exactly these units ('FIX-HELD-DUP: on the hosting area - already in enemy_oc'). (b) Reach is measured to 3.79" of the marker, not to the area, so enemy units one move from the area edge are missed. (c) on_other also uses marker distance. I re-computed this statically over the 275 saved movement positions in 40k/tests/rollout_cases. In 16 of 74 held-threatened objectives some enemy OC is counted twice; examples: s7459 r2 P2 centre, 18 of the 20 threat OC come from a Beast Snagga unit already on the area; s7462 r3 P2 centre, 15 of 38. In 45 of 74, area reach is missed. Over 52 one-move reinforcement candidates, RI-RACE fires 4 times as coded and 12 times with an area-correct count (8 disagree). The design's premise ('measured from the nearest model, as control is') is not the engine's control test in the bench. This is the same kind of threat-count error that sank round 3's REINFORCE-CAP. The unit test uses marker-only objectives, so it cannot catch this.

When hd_obj is non-empty, measure each alive model's gap with hd_mm.model_gap_to_objective_range_px(model, hd_obj) (0 when on the area); otherwise use marker distance minus CR. Count the unit when the gap is at most (M+2)". Set on_other with _unit_in_objective_range against the other objectives' board entries, keeping the marker test only as a fallback. Add a test with hosting-area objectives (source_pieces plus a stub mm) asserting two things: an enemy on the area more than 3.79" from the marker is not counted twice, and an enemy one move from the area edge is counted. Then re-run s7437 and the guardrails, since firing roughly triples on the saved positions and the 1.5 ratio may need re-checking.

reviews.summary:
The root design is a sound idea, cleanly gated and well tested: an [ASSAULT]-aware long-trip Advance, a race test for one-move reinforcements, and table quarters priced in VP. It flips s7437 r2 to the measured alternative (Beta Advances to obj_nml_2). My static re-computation agrees with its trigger values there (27 vs 17 enemy OC, quarter_vp 9.0).

Verdict is revise because of one real bug in its central new piece. RI-RACE's threat count measures to the 3.79" marker range. Control in every bench objective is the 11e hosting area (7x11.5" areas, FIX_HELD_DUP on). Enemy units already on the area away from the marker are counted twice; COORD-5 already excludes them. Units that can reach the area edge are missed. On 275 saved positions the as-coded trigger fires 4 of 52 times against 12 with an area-correct count. The fix is to use _unit_in_objective_range and model_gap_to_objective_range_px, then add a hosting-area test case.

The design does not touch s7451: that walk came from the COORD-4 support pass. In the bench, the effect will be driven mainly by RI-ASSAULT on the 6 Custodian Guard units per Custodes list. It is uncounted in the report and shares the reinforcement switch, so it should get its own param and bench arm before a bundle result can be read. RI-QUARTER only plays in about 2 of 25 seeds and credits the same quarter to every unit in the once-per-phase plan.

scores.note: Flips s7437 to the measured alternative (Beta Advances to obj_nml_2). Test fails on base (5) and passes on the fix. The guardrails are unchanged, but s7424 r3 p1 was not checked. The flip rests on RI-RACE (centre 48.2 -> 34.8), not on the quarter tier the A/B measured: RI-QUARTER adds only 9.0, and without RI-RACE 48.2 > 38.3. RI-RACE measures reach to the marker, but control is decided by the 11e hosting area, so it double-counts enemies on the area and misses reach to the area edge. With an area-correct count it still fires at s7437 (42 vs 17). RI-ASSAULT shares the one switch and changes most Custodes bench games. Its cited in-band evidence (s7420 r2 P2, +8.94) is not reachable by the patch: the gap is 15.8" at M8, so Advancing cannot save a turn. RI-QUARTER counts the mover's attached leader as another unit (this flaw was not flagged for this design). Param 0 restores base exactly; values are cached. The RI-ASSAULT log line prints even when base would Advance anyway.

Exact s7437 flip through the measured quarter-tier mechanism, with no score changes and param 0 = base. Test fails on base (4) and passes on the fix. All 6 guardrails were checked, including s7424, but finding 2's card is misstated. It is a special-case pass-2 gate: the flat 4.2 quarter bonus (which also rewards points near the centre) and the [ASSAULT] long-trip test stay wrong everywhere else. Other flaws: the mover's attached leader counts as covering the old quarter; coverage ignores the plan's own moves, so several reinforcers can be stripped from one held objective; it assumes a full-M walk and an M+3.5 Advance that the executor does not make; it Advances without checking the shooting or charge cost. It changes only about 3-6 of 124 bench pairs, the keeper-fix outcome.

Right idea for Reconnaissance Sweep: quarters priced at card VP with the scorer's presence test, a free [ASSAULT] Advance into the quarter, and an exemption from the race vetoes. The s7437 flip is exact (52.8 vs 48.2). But Engage on All Fronts is priced as if it paid every turn, while the bench's tactical deck pays it once: 3 VP is valued at 21-31.5 points. That path drives most of its bench changes (EoAF is held in about 16% of pairs). At s7454 r3 P2 (clear +21.5, n36, P2 holds EoAF) it adds +21 to the move that measured worse. Attached leaders are counted both ways: a led squad gets no value for staying, and leaving its quarter is credited as a phantom tier. The strong persistence weights can hold units in quarters. The exemption ignores claims. The report omits EoAF activity at s7438 and the s7424 guardrail, and the test never exercises the exemption the flip depends on.

verdict.reasons:
No design is disqualified. All three flip s7437 r2 P1 to the measured alternative: Custodian Guard Beta Advances to obj_nml_2, the same unit, objective and mode. Each test fails on base and passes on the fix. No guardrail moves toward a harmful alternative. None of them reaches the extra evidence at s7451 (+5.86): that walk comes from the pass-3 support move (_find_best_remaining_objective), which only ever returns move or hold.

Root wins, narrowly.
- It implements all three directions the brief lists, each as an extension of existing logic:
  - a RACE-1-style race test for one-move reinforcements, with reach measured from the nearest model;
  - the 11e [ASSAULT] exception in RACE-1's long-trip Advance test;
  - Reconnaissance Sweep tiers priced with the scorer's own presence test, replacing the flat 4.2 that also rewarded points within 6" of the centre.
- Its two major review issues (marker-based reach in RI-RACE, one switch for three parts) are local fixes that keep the flip. With area-correct reach, RI-RACE still fires at s7437 (42 vs 17 OC).
- It is the only design that changes enough bench games to be measured.
- It holds no units back (the round-2 pattern). RI-RACE's remaining gaps (M+2 reach instead of Advance reach, holders that charge off still counted) make it fire less, not wrongly, so it does not repeat REINFORCE-CAP's blind spot.

It is not a clean win, and the required changes follow from its weak points:
- The s7437 flip rests on RI-RACE, not on the quarter tier the A/B measured.
- RI-ASSAULT is broad and has no measured support beyond s7437. The s7420 position cited for it is unreachable: Advancing there cannot save a turn.
- RI-QUARTER counts attached leaders as other units. This has no bench impact (the fixtures have no attachments) but is wrong in real games.

Narrow is the safest design: an exact flip through the measured mechanism, with no score changes. But it is a special-case gate that leaves the flawed quarter pricing and the [ASSAULT] test in place, and it changes about 3-6 of 124 bench pairs.

Game has the best Reconnaissance Sweep valuation, but it ships an Engage on All Fronts path priced as recurring. That path is about 2-3x too high in the tactical deck, drives most of its bench changes, and is contradicted by s7454 r3 P2. That puts it last.

I did not run Godot. Every finding above comes from reading the code and running Python over the saved positions.
required_changes: Split the switch. Add FIX_RI_RACE, FIX_RI_ASSAULT and FIX_RI_QUARTER (each 1.0, read with get_param at its own branch) and keep FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE as a master (0 = base exactly for all three). Extend test_param_zero_restores_base to all three parts: at 0 the [ASSAULT] case walks 3 turns and the flat 4.2 secondary_spread returns.

RI-RACE on 11e hosting areas. Pass hd_obj_by_id[obj_id], hd_mm and the other objectives' board entries into _ri_enemy_next_move_oc. Skip an enemy unit when _unit_in_objective_range(e_unit, hd_obj, hd_mm) is true (it is already in eval.enemy_oc; COORD-5 skips it the same way). Measure each alive model's gap with hd_mm.model_gap_to_objective_range_px(model, hd_obj) and count the unit when the gap is at most (M+2)" (use marker distance minus CR only when hd_obj is empty). Set on_other with _unit_in_objective_range against the other objectives. Add a test with source_pieces objectives: an enemy on the area more than 3.79" from the marker is counted once, and an enemy one move from the area edge is counted. Then re-verify that s7437 still fires (area-correct count is 42 vs 17) and re-run the guardrails.

RI-QUARTER coverage. After ri_others.erase(unit_id), also erase every id in unit.attachment_data.attached_characters, and any unit embarked in it, because they move with the unit. Use a zero offset for already_on_obj candidates, and the Advance pace for any candidate whose action is 'advance' (the gap in (M, M+2] case). Add a test where a led squad and its leader are the only cover of a quarter: moving into another uncovered quarter gets no quarter_vp.

RI-ASSAULT logging and guard. Print the RI-ASSAULT line only when an enemy centroid is within max_weapon_range (the only case where base refuses), so the log count equals the number of changed long-trip decisions. In that branch, also require no enemy within M+12" unless flags.effect_advance_and_charge is set. Otherwise units whose advance-and-charge comes only from ability text (Wazdakka's Waaagh!) skip base's charge-reach guard and start Advancing past a possible charge in the Ork fixtures.
grafts: Carry the s7437 decision on the quarter mechanism the A/B measured, not only on RI-RACE. Options: (a) game's RACE-SKIP/TOO-LATE exemption for a candidate that takes an uncovered quarter this turn; (b) a higher RI-QUARTER weight (game used 3.5 score per VP), measured in a forced Reconnaissance Sweep arm; (c) narrow's REINFORCE-INSURANCE pass-2 gate as the fallback if the RI-RACE-off arm is not positive.

From narrow: a pass-2 quarter ledger. Once a candidate whose end spot takes uncovered quarter Q is assigned, later candidates that end in Q lose quarter_vp, so several units are not credited for one quarter.

Step value toward a tier: tier_vp / (quarters still missing) for a new quarter that does not yet complete a tier. Custodes, which start in one quarter, then keep a round-1 pull under Reconnaissance Sweep after the flat 4.2 is removed.

RI-RACE: apply MOVE_RACE_LOSS_FACTOR only to the command-phase hold value, or skip the halving while an end-of-our-turn central rule is active (Centre Ground, hold_central eot). Also skip it when no enemy turn follows (P2 in round 5). Optionally measure an Advance-reach variant (M+3.5").
